title: Apparently I Am Now the kingdom’s least qualified problem solver and Now Everyone Thinks I Am Important
synopsis: A part-time villain accepts a mysterious job and discovers that the job is to manage the hero's retirement fund. The story unfolds in The Inland Sea of Forty-Nine Mayors, where a promise spoken beside water becomes magically enforceable. The central problem is a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization. Toma Voss wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A part-time villain accepts a mysterious job and discovers that the job is to manage the hero's retirement fund.
authorNotes: Every coincidence is intentional. Every typo is probably a prophecy.

chapters.title: My Completely Reasonable Plan To the Extremely Suspicious Cake — Toma Voss POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Toma Voss POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Toma Voss arrived at the ministry basement intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
Nothing attacks anyone, which makes the characters more nervous than usual.
Toma Voss regarded the situation with the professional disappointment of someone who had already predicted it.
The important object was a permit. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Toma Voss checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Inland Sea of Forty-Nine Mayors followed one inconvenient rule: A promise spoken beside water becomes magically enforceable.
Nothing happened for several minutes. The silence became so suspicious that somebody checked the ceiling.
This was technically progress. Unfortunately, it was progress in the wrong direction.
A second person arrived carrying information about the unexplained border change. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the permit. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Toma Voss wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Toma Voss has a private connection to the missing relic.
The mystery remained open, although Toma Voss now had one useful fact: someone was treating the unexplained border change as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Toma Voss made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
